newsitem.title: GERMANY: China's airports threaten HK as cargo hub - agent.
newsitem.headline: China's airports threaten HK as cargo hub - agent.

text.p: The future of Hong Kong as an air cargo hub could be threatened by the growth of nearby airports within China, Air China's German cargo sales agent Penta Shipping GmbH said.

Frank Wortmann, Penta Shipping managing director, forecast Hong Kong would gradually lose its role as a transshipment hub for southern China despite the forthcoming opening of the territory's new Chep Lap Kok airport.
Other southern Chinese airports such as Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Macau would increasingly gain direct connections, he told Reuters in an interview.
"There are five airports in a radius of about 200 miles and this capacity is not necessary. I do not know if there is a need for the new Hong Kong airport," Wortmann said..
"The Martinair flight (Amsterdam to Guangzhou) is the start of a trend," he predicted.
Martinair N.V. plans a twice-weekly freighter flight to Guangzhou starting later in October, the first such service by a European airline. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
